UPSTREAM: acpi: Sort the reported APIC-IDs in the MADT table coreboot performs MP-Init in a parallel way. That leads to the fact that the order, in which the CPUs are woken up, can vary from boot to boot. The creation of the MADT table just parses the devicetree and takes the CPUs reported there as it is for creating the single local APIC entries. Therefore, the OS will see different order of CPUs. There are CPUs out there (like Apollo Lake for example) which have shared caches on core-level and if the order is random this can end up in assigning cores to different tasks or even OSes (in a virtual environment) which uses the same cache. This in turn will produce performance penalties across these distributed tasks/OSes. Though there is a way to discover the core- and cache-topology it will in the end be necessary to take the APIC-ID into account. To simplify it, one can achieve the same output by sorting the APIC-IDs in an ascending order. This will lead to the fact that CPUs that share a given cache will be reported right next to each other in the MADT. UPSTREAM: soc/intel/cannonlake: Disable ACPI mode as part of pmc_soc_init PMC initialization on Cannon Lake happens earlier in the boot sequence than other SoCs because FSP-Silicon init hides PMC from PCI bus. As ACPI disabling was done as part of PMC init, it was being called earlier than what other SoCs do. This resulted in a different order of events for some drivers e.g. ChromeOS EC. In case of ChromeOS EC, it ended up clearing EC events (which happens as part of ACPI disabling in SMM) before logging any events of interest that happen during mainboard initialization. This change moves the call to disable ACPI to pmc_soc_init just like other SoCs to keep the order of events more aligned. UPSTREAM: soc/intel/cannonlake: Add a config for configuring SD_VDD1_PWR_EN# SD controller in CNL-PCH provides a ability to configure the behavior of SD_VDD1_PWR_EN# as an active high or low signal. FSP provides an UPD "SdCardPowerEnableActiveHigh" to control the same. However, for platforms using SD_VDD1_PWR_EN# as active high, the SDXC card connector is always powered and may impact system power. This is because SD_VDD1_PWR_EN# does not de-assert during SDXC D3 or when SD card is not inserted. Workaround is to change the pad ownership of SD_VDD1_PWR_EN to GPIO and force the TX buffer to low in _PS3. And restore the pad mode to native function in _PS0. Hence add a Kconfig option to update the UPD, which the board can select based on how the SD_VDD1_PWR_EN is implemented on it. And, the workaround gets applied based on this config. CHROMIUM: cros_ec: use ODR events to clear the spreading history This uses the ODR flag introduced in CL:1450288 to clear the last batch data used by the spreading algorithm. The spreading code relies on accurately measuring the effective interval between batches of samples. An ODR change means that the previous batches may no longer represent the behavior of the EC. If an ODR change is immediately followed by a batch, the AP will attempt to spread based on the previous interval, which can easily lead to "spreading into the future", leading to subsequent timestamp mismatch errors. This patch solves that problem by having ODR events be breaking points for the spreading code. The tradeoff is that this can cause samples to be lost immediately after an ODR change. This problem can't effectively be solved without either: - storing those samples in a side queue and spreading them once updated information becomes available to do so; - communicating the ODR to the AP as part of the ODR event. sepolicy: add type_transistion when chromeos_domain creating under /var Use type_transistion to make sure creating directory "lib" under any directory labelled as cros_var are automatically labelled as cros_var_lib, and vice-versa for "cache", "log", etc. Directories under /var/ like /var/lib, /var/spool, may be deleted and re-created during running of the system, including tests. Previously, we have `restorecon -R -D /var` to fixing SELinux file labels under /var upon boot. But `-D` options makes it only tries to fix when the policy has changed, for example, policy upgrades along with OTA. Recreated /var/lib won't be "fixed" upon any reboot unless the policy has changed. The major reason for not to attempt relabelling everytime is recursive relabelling takes time, and this will slow down Chrome OS boot process. Also, relabelling shouldn't be necessary unless the policy has changed if everything is functioning well. moblab-generic-vm-paladin provision_AutoUpdate has encourterd the situation that after AutoUpdate, files under /var/lib including /var/lib itself is not correctly labeled, because there's no policy upgrade. restorecon simply skips everything to not to slow down boot process with a recursive relabelling, which does nothing most of the time. crrev.com/c/1450654 provides an emergency workaround "fix" like `restorecon -R -D /var/*` which expands to `retorecon -R -D /var/lib /var/cache /var/log ...`, since the last policy is stored at the xattr of the specified directory inode, recreated /var/lib will be treated as relabeling needed since no last policy hash is stored at /var/lib, but only at /var. type_transistion will be the long term fix to let kernel correctly recreate the directory with correct label, and leaving `restorecon -R -D /var` for policy upgrades, or first policy introduction purpose only. FROMLIST: [v3] driver: platform: Support parsing GpioInt 0 in platform_get_irq() ACPI 5 added support for GpioInt resources as a way to provide information about interrupts mediated via a GPIO controller. Several device buses (e.g. SPI, I2C) have support for retrieving an IRQ specified via this type of resource, and providing it directly to the driver as an IRQ number. This is not currently done for the platform drivers, as platform_get_irq() does not try to parse GpioInt() resources. This requires drivers to either have to support only one possible IRQ resource, or to have code in place to try both as a failsafe. While there is a possibility of ambiguity for devices that exposes multiple IRQs, it is easy and feasible to support the common case of devices that only expose one IRQ which would be of either type depending on the underlying system's architecture. This commit adds support for parsing a GpioInt resource in order to fulfill a request for the index 0 IRQ for a platform device. from: https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10824703/ BUG=b:123750725 TEST=boot Kasumi360, observe GPIO work Change-Id: Ibbc9d78546c8189b08d30fd501747ee19bb180f0 Signed-off-by: Enrico Granata <egranata@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1483850 Tested-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Raul E Rangel <rrangel@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benjamin Gordon <bmgordon@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: add vmstat counts for different page fault types VM event counters are added to keep track of anonymous vs. file vs. shmem page faults. They are: pgmajfault_a, pgmajfault_f and pgmajfault_s. These are useful to analyze system performance, particularly when the cost of a fault for a file page is very different from that of an anonymous page, as would happen, for instance, in the presence of zram. The PGMAJFAULT counter is no longer directly maintained, for performance. Instead the three new counters are added whenever the total count is needed. This adds entries to /proc/vmstat. vm_tools: maitred: max stateful fs size at boot As a first step toward more dynamic stateful disk sizing, add a btrfs online resize operation to maximize the filesystem within its block device. This will take place on each boot, but it should have minimal overhead if the block device size has not changed (less than 10 ms) and should not take a significant amount of time even when actually resizing, since this will always be expanding into new free space, which doesn't require any shuffling of existing data (growing a 1 GB FS to 2 GB takes less than 100 ms on my test system). Note that this will only work for expanding the disk image; it is not safe to shrink the disk image unless the filesystem is shrunk first, which will never happen in this code path due to the use of 'max' as the size specifier. The approach taken here is enough to allow the virtual block device image to be resized to let the VM consume newly-available free space that wasn't available at VM creation time. Shrinking the VM disk image would need to issue a BTRFS resize operation with an absolute size specified, followed by shrinking the disk image file to that size. However, since we use a sparse backing file for the stateful disk image, free space should already be reclaimed from the VM even if the logical disk size is larger than the available space. Tested by manually expanding the stateful disk image with truncate(1) and restarting the VM, observing the change in filesystem size. shill: simplfy Nl80211Frame::ToString() Nl80211Frame::ToString() returns a boolean and appends the result to the provided std::string* argument. The only scenario that it returns false is when the std::string* argument is null. Instead, this CL simplifies Nl80211Frame::ToString() to return a std::string and let the caller to append the returned string to another std::string if needed. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests.
